regression_risk_analysis.evidence: §7 'Layer-differentiation gloss' explicitly addresses codex iter-1's regression-trap warning: 'Codex's worry was not L3 is wrong layer but L3 changes touching the same file simultaneously collide. Cycle 8 addresses that by (a) reducing N from 4→3, (b) sequencing the 3 to land in a deterministic order (§9), (c) requiring all 8 baseline + ~15 new fixtures to stay green at every intermediate state.' §9 phases the 3 items 8.1→8.2→8.3 with validation gates between each. §14 enumerates 10 specific risk vectors with named defenses: R1 signature-change call sites, R2 label-normalization vs inline links, R3 footnote-vs-shortcut-ref [^/non-^ disambiguation], R4 unclosed <details>, R5 abbr single-quote, R6 popover state leak, R7 def-line false-positive, R8 details without summary, R9 800-line budget, R10 no-codex this cycle. Each has explicit fixture-level guard.
regression_risk_analysis.notes: The mitigation is credible: (1) Phase 8.1 lands ref-links first because that probe ALSO validates the 2-pass def-collection pattern with the lowest blast radius (no new render components). (2) Phase 8.2 reuses the def-collection pattern — incremental risk only. (3) Phase 8.3 lands HTML inline with a known-good consumeKbdSpan template + the most invasive piece (<details> block) last so prior phases are stable. R3 is the highest-risk inline-token collision and the spec resolves it deterministically (^-prefix gate).
